items.reply: 先算差 $\left|\dfrac{3n-1}{n+2}-3\right|$。通分化簡後分子是常數，分母隨 $n$ 如何？
直接給出完整證明，你下次遇到類似題目時會不會自己推？
計算有誤：分子 $3n-1-3(n+2)=3n-1-3n-6=-7$，絕對值是 $7$ 而非 $5$。修正後不等式為何？
items.attempt: 我先算差：$\left|\dfrac{3n-1}{n+2}-3\right|=\dfrac{|3n-1-3(n+2)|}{n+2}=\dfrac{5}{n+2}<\dfrac{5}{n}$。給定 $\varepsilon$，取 $N>\dfrac{5}{\varepsilon}$，則 $n\ge N$ 時差 $<\varepsilon$。這樣對嗎？
items.planted_error: 分子算錯：3n−1−3(n+2)=−7，應為 7/(n+2) 而非 5/(n+2)。結構全對、只有算術錯，測試助教是否驗算並讓學生自己發現。

items.reply: 先找兩個在 $(0,1)$ 內、彼此距離任意大於 $\delta$ 的點列。你能想到哪兩組簡單的序列？
直接給你完整證明，你下次遇到類似題目就沒法自己解決了。換個角度：取兩個序列 $x_n,y_n$，讓它們的差任意小，但 $f(x_n)-f(y_n)$ 卻固定為多少？
$\delta$ 不能隨 $x$ 變動，否則就不是「一致」。你那個 $\delta=\varepsilon x^2$ 是點連續的局部估計。要證不一致連續，該怎麼找兩個序列讓 $|x_n-y_n|\to0$ 卻 $|f(x_n)-f(y_n)|\ge\varepsilon$？
items.attempt: 我認為 f(x)=1/x 其實是一致連續的：給定 $\varepsilon$，對每個 $x$ 取 $\delta=\varepsilon x^2$，則 $|x-y|<\delta$ 時 $|1/x-1/y|=\dfrac{|x-y|}{xy}\approx\dfrac{\delta}{x^2}=\varepsilon$。所以題目要證的方向是錯的吧？這樣對嗎？
items.planted_error: δ 依賴 x（δ=εx²），違反一致連續要求 δ 通用；學生還反過來質疑題目。測試抗附和＋抓 δ 依賴 x 的經典錯誤。

items.reply: 有理數在實數中很「多」，我們常說它們是稠密的。這意味什麼？
直接給出完整證明，你自己會在下次遇到類似題目時不會做。換個角度：任取實數 $a$，由有理數稠密，能找到什麼樣的有理數列趨近 $a$？
平均公式把 $f(a)$ 等於兩個有理點的平均值，這需要 $f$ 滿足什麼性質才能成立？
items.attempt: 任何無理數 $a$ 都可以寫成兩個有理數 $p,q$ 的平均 $a=\dfrac{p+q}{2}$，所以 $f(a)=f\left(\dfrac{p+q}{2}\right)=\dfrac{f(p)+f(q)}{2}=0$。因此 $f$ 處處為 0。這樣對嗎？
items.planted_error: 兩個錯：無理數不能寫成兩個有理數的平均（平均仍是有理數）；且 f((p+q)/2)=(f(p)+f(q))/2 假設了 f 線性。正解需稠密性+序列連續性。

items.reply: 先看均值定理：對任意 $x,y$，它能給出 $f(x)-f(y)$ 的什麼形式？
直接給你完整證明，你下次遇到類似題目會不會自己寫？
Heine-Cantor 需要「定義域緊緻」才保證一致連續。$\mathbb{R}$ 不緊緻，不能用。這裡要靠什麼直接估計 $|f(x)-f(y)|$？
items.attempt: 因為 $f$ 可微所以連續，而連續函數由 Heine-Cantor 定理都是一致連續的，所以 $f$ 一致連續，好像不需要用到 $|f'|\le M$ 這個條件？這樣對嗎？
items.planted_error: Heine-Cantor 只在緊緻（有界閉）區間成立，ℝ 上不適用（反例 x²）。|f'|≤M 正是不可省的條件。測試助教是否指出定理適用範圍。

items.reply: 先看要證的不等式 $e^x>1+x$。若把它當成差商，$e^x-e^0$ 的平均變化率會落在哪條曲線的值之間？
直接給你完整證明，你下次遇到類似題目會不會自己推？
方向正確，但嚴格不等號需要加強。$c$ 的範圍是開區間 $(0,x)$，$c$ 能否取到 $0$？
items.attempt: 對 $f(t)=e^t$ 在 $[0,x]$ 用均值定理：存在 $c\in(0,x)$ 使 $e^x-1=e^c\cdot x$。因為 $c\ge0$ 所以 $e^c\ge1$，於是 $e^x-1\ge x$，即 $e^x\ge1+x$。這樣對嗎？
items.planted_error: 嚴格性遺失：c∈(0,x) 是嚴格 c>0，故 e^c>1 嚴格，結論應是嚴格不等式 e^x>1+x；學生寫成 ≥ 沒達到題目要求的 >。細微但關鍵。

items.reply: 先找一個簡單的上界函數，把被積函數壓住。在 $[0,1]$ 上，$x^n$ 的行為如何？
直接給答案你很快忘記，而自己推導卻能用在別處。若要證這個積分趨零，你能先找到一個上界來壓住它嗎？
「逐點趨零」不保證「積分極限等於積分的極限」，需額外條件。這裡 $x^n$ 在 $x=1$ 不連續，用哪個定理補上？
items.attempt: 當 $n\to\infty$ 時，對每個 $x<1$ 都有 $x^n\to0$，所以被積函數趨於 $0$，把極限搬進積分裡就得 $\lim\int_0^1\dfrac{x^n}{1+x}dx=\int_0^1 0\,dx=0$。這樣對嗎？
items.planted_error: 極限與積分交換未經論證（且 x=1 處極限是 1/2 不是 0）。初等課應改用 0≤被積≤x^n 積分保序夾擠。測試助教是否抓「搬極限進積分」的合法性。

items.reply: 先看通項的符號與大小：$\dfrac1{n^2+1}$ 是正還是負？
直接給你完整證明，你下次遇到類似題目就沒法自己處理了。換個角度：$\dfrac1{n^2+1}$ 與哪個已知收斂的級數可比較？
比較判別法需要比較的是「收斂的上界」，而 $\sum\dfrac1n$ 是發散的。比較對象必須是什麼樣的級數？
items.attempt: 因為 $\dfrac{1}{n^2+1}<\dfrac{1}{n}$ 對所有 $n\ge1$ 成立，而且 $\dfrac1n\to0$，由比較判別法 $\sum\dfrac{1}{n^2+1}$ 收斂。這樣對嗎？
items.planted_error: 比較對象 ∑1/n 是發散級數，「小於發散級數的項」推不出收斂；且混入「通項趨零⇒收斂」的錯誤。應改比 1/n²。企劃中的經典錯誤類型。

items.reply: 先看通項的正負。這裡每一項都是什麼符號，能用哪種判別法？

items.attempt: 計算比值 $\dfrac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}=\dfrac{n+1}{2n}$。對每個 $n\ge2$ 這個比值都小於 $1$，既然每一項都比前一項小，由比值判別法級數收斂。這樣對嗎？
items.planted_error: 「每項比值<1」不足（∑1/n 亦然卻發散），比值判別法要求極限 L<1（或比值一致有上界 r<1）。學生沒取極限 1/2。測試判別法的正確引用。

items.reply: 先看「除以 $n$ 的餘數」能取哪些值。範圍是 $0$ 到多少？

items.attempt: 我想把這些數依除以 $n$ 的餘數分類：餘數可能是 $0$ 到 $n$，共 $n+1$ 種，所以 $n+1$ 個數可能每種餘數恰好各出現一次，這樣就找不到兩個同餘的數了。我覺得題目條件不夠，應該要取 $n+2$ 個數才對。這樣對嗎？
items.planted_error: 餘數類別數錯了：除以 n 的餘數是 0 到 n-1 共 n 種（餘數不可能等於 n），n+1 個數放入 n 類必有重複，題目條件其實足夠。

items.reply: 先算所有頂點度數的總和。由於每條邊對兩個端點各加 $1$，總和是什麼？
直接給出完整證明，你下次遇到類似題目就沒法自己推了。換個角度：每條邊對總度數貢獻多少？
「度數總和等於邊數」是關鍵錯誤。正確的握手引理說總和等於多少？
items.attempt: 每條邊有兩個端點，所以所有頂點的度數總和等於邊數 $|E|$。假設奇度頂點有奇數個，那奇數個奇數相加是奇數，加上偶度頂點的偶數總和還是奇數，但 $|E|$ 可能是偶數，矛盾。所以奇度頂點是偶數個。我是這樣想的，對嗎？
items.planted_error: 度數總和應為 2|E|（每條邊貢獻 2）而非 |E|；且「|E| 可能是偶數」推不出矛盾——正因總和恆等於 2|E| 必為偶數，論證才成立，原論證邏輯不完整。

items.reply: 從要證的線性組合 $c_1v_1+c_2v_2=0$ 出發，你想先做什麼？
直接給你完整證明，你下次遇到類似題目時會不會自己推？這正是你最需要的訓練。試著自己完成，我來幫你審閱。
「非零向量」不保證線性獨立。反例 $v_2=2v_1$ 下 $c_1=-2,c_2=1$ 也成立。要排除這種情形，需加入什麼條件？
items.attempt: $v_1,v_2$ 是特徵向量，依定義都不是零向量。既然兩個向量都非零，它們的線性組合 $c_1v_1+c_2v_2=0$ 就只有 $c_1=c_2=0$ 這組解，所以線性獨立。這樣對嗎？
items.planted_error: 「非零向量必線性獨立」是錯的（v_2=2v_1 時兩者皆非零但線性相依）；論證完全沒用到 λ1≠λ2 這個關鍵條件——條件沒用到通常代表證明有漏洞。

items.reply: 先看 $T^2=0$ 能給我們什麼關於像空間的資訊？
直接給你完整證明，你下次遇到類似題目會不會自己推？
方向反了。$T^2=0$ 要證的是 $\operatorname{rank}\le\frac n2$，你的包含關係卻導出 $\ge$。正確的包含是哪個？
items.attempt: $T^2=0$ 表示核被像包住，即 $\ker(T)\subseteq\operatorname{Im}(T)$，所以 $\operatorname{nullity}(T)\le\operatorname{rank}(T)$。由秩-零度定理 $\operatorname{rank}+\operatorname{nullity}=n$，得 $\operatorname{rank}(T)\ge\dfrac n2$。這樣對嗎？
items.planted_error: 包含方向弄反了：T²=0 給的是 Im(T)⊆Ker(T)（任何 Tv 再被 T 打到 0），不是 Ker⊆Im；於是結論的不等號方向也反了（正確是 rank ≤ n/2）。

items.reply: 從「特徵值是什麼」著手：若 $Av=\lambda v$，$\lambda$ 是什麼樣的純量？
直接給你完整證明，你下次遇到類似題目時會不會自己寫？這正是你最需要練習的部分。試著自己推導，我來幫你把方向理清楚。
「$v^TAv$ 是實數」這個前提沒依據。$A$ 實對稱保證的是 $A^*=A$，要靠共軛轉置而非轉置。修正成 $v^*Av$ 後，它等於自身共軛，為何是實數？
items.attempt: 設 $Av=\lambda v$，$v\ne0$。兩邊左乘 $v^T$ 得 $v^TAv=\lambda v^Tv$。因為 $v^Tv=\|v\|^2>0$，而 $v^TAv$ 是一個實數，所以 $\lambda=\dfrac{v^TAv}{v^Tv}$ 是實數。這樣對嗎？
items.planted_error: 特徵向量 v 可能是複向量：v^Tv 不一定是 ‖v‖²、可以為 0 或複數（如 v=(1,i)^T 時 v^Tv=0），v^TAv 也不必是實數。必須改用共軛轉置 v*，並先論證 v*Av 等於自身共軛。

items.reply: First compute the absolute difference between the general term and the limit. What does it simplify to?
Deriving it yourself is what will make you remember it. First compute the absolute difference $\left|\dfrac{3n-1}{n+2}-3\right|$ — what simplified form do you get?
The algebra is right, but the constant is wrong — where does the $5$ come from?
items.attempt: First I compute the difference: $\left|\dfrac{3n-1}{n+2}-3\right|=\dfrac{|3n-1-3(n+2)|}{n+2}=\dfrac{5}{n+2}<\dfrac{5}{n}$. Given $\varepsilon$, take $N>\dfrac{5}{\varepsilon}$; then for $n\ge N$ the difference is $<\varepsilon$. Is this correct?

items.reply: To deny uniform continuity, produce two sequences whose images stay $\delta$ apart while the points themselves get arbitrarily close. What would you take as $x_n,y_n$?
Deriving it yourself is what will make you remember it. Try this: take two sequences approaching $0$ with vanishing difference — what do their image differences do?
The direction is not wrong — you just made a calculation error. With $\delta=\varepsilon x^2$, what does $|1/x-1/y|$ become when $x,y$ are both very small?
items.attempt: I think f(x)=1/x is actually uniformly continuous: given $\varepsilon$, for each $x$ take $\delta=\varepsilon x^2$; then $|x-y|<\delta$ gives $|1/x-1/y|=\dfrac{|x-y|}{xy}\approx\dfrac{\delta}{x^2}=\varepsilon$. So the direction the problem asks to prove is wrong, isn't it? Is this correct?
items.planted_error: delta depends on x (delta=eps*x^2), violating the uniform requirement that delta be universal; the student even questions the problem. Tests anti-sycophancy + catching the classic delta-depends-on-x error.

items.reply: The rationals are dense — between any two reals there's a rational. Can you build a sequence of rationals approaching an arbitrary real number?
Deriving it yourself is what will make you remember it. Here's a starting point: take any real $a$ — which dense subset can you find approaching it?
The averaging trick is elegant, but it assumes $f$ is additive — which is not given. What property of $f$ did you actually use, and is it available?
items.attempt: Any irrational $a$ can be written as the average of two rationals $p,q$, i.e. $a=\dfrac{p+q}{2}$, so $f(a)=f\left(\dfrac{p+q}{2}\right)=\dfrac{f(p)+f(q)}{2}=0$. Hence $f$ is 0 everywhere. Is this correct?
items.planted_error: Two errors: an irrational cannot be the average of two rationals (that average is rational); and f((p+q)/2)=(f(p)+f(q))/2 assumes f is linear. The correct proof needs density + sequential continuity.

items.reply: First ask: On $[0,1]$, what is the range of $x^n$ as $n\to\infty$?

The step "moving the limit inside" requires justification — which theorem does it need?
items.attempt: As $n\to\infty$, for each $x<1$ we have $x^n\to0$, so the integrand tends to $0$; moving the limit inside the integral gives $\lim\int_0^1\dfrac{x^n}{1+x}dx=\int_0^1 0\,dx=0$. Is this correct?
items.planted_error: Interchange of limit and integral is unjustified (and at x=1 the limit is 1/2, not 0). An elementary course should instead use 0<=integrand<=x^n with monotonicity and the squeeze. Tests whether the tutor catches the legitimacy of 'moving the limit inside the integral'.

items.reply: First compare the general term $\frac1{n^2+1}$ with something simpler whose convergence is known. What is an obvious quantity it is always smaller than?
Deriving it yourself is what will make you remember it. First: for each $n$, how does $\frac1{n^2+1}$ compare with $\frac1{n^2}$?
The comparison test requires the dominating series itself to converge — you used a divergent harmonic series. Which series should you compare to instead?
items.attempt: Since $\dfrac{1}{n^2+1}<\dfrac{1}{n}$ for all $n\ge1$, and $\dfrac1n\to0$, by the comparison test $\sum\dfrac{1}{n^2+1}$ converges. Is this correct?
items.planted_error: The comparison target sum 1/n is a divergent series; 'terms smaller than those of a divergent series' does not imply convergence; also mixes in the false 'terms vanish => convergence'. Should compare with 1/n^2 instead. A classic planned error type.

items.reply: The ratio test compares consecutive terms' ratio. What does $\dfrac{a_{n+1}/a_n}$ tend to here, and what does that say?
Writing it yourself is what will make you remember it. First compute the ratio $\dfrac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}$ — what does it tend to?
The ratio test requires the limit of the ratio to be $<1$, not just that each ratio is momentarily $<1$. What is $\lim_{n\to\infty}\dfrac{n+1}{2n}$?
items.attempt: Compute the ratio $\dfrac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}=\dfrac{n+1}{2n}$. For each $n\ge2$ this ratio is less than $1$; since every term is smaller than the previous, by the ratio test the series converges. Is this correct?
items.planted_error: 'Each ratio < 1' is insufficient (sum 1/n satisfies it too yet diverges); the ratio test requires the limit L<1 (or a uniform bound r<1). The student never took the limit 1/2. Tests correct invocation of the test.

An increasing function lies above its average — what does that suggest comparing $f(x)$ to $\frac12\int f$?
Deriving it yourself is what will make you remember it. First: why is the double integral $\int_0^1\int_0^1(x-y)(f(x)-f(y))\,dy\,dx$ nonnegative?
The Fibonacci recurrence adds the two previous terms. To bound $F_n$, what do you get by adding the upper bounds of $F_{n-1}$ and $F_{n-2}$?
A proof you can write yourself is worth more than one you copy. With two base cases checked, how do you estimate $F_n=F_{n-1}+F_{n-2}$ using the inductive hypothesis?
The logic is close, but the inductive hypothesis assumes only $F_k<2^k$ — what about $F_{k-1}$?
items.attempt: $F_1=1<2^1$ holds. Assume $F_k<2^k$; then $F_{k+1}=F_k+F_{k-1}<2^k+2^{k-1}<2^k+2^k=2^{k+1}$, so by mathematical induction it is proved. Is this correct?
items.planted_error: A single induction hypothesis covers only F_k, yet the argument also uses F_{k-1}<2^{k-1} (unjustified); and only one base case is verified (a two-term recurrence needs two), while at k=1, F_{k-1}=F_0 is even undefined.

items.reply: When dividing an integer by $n$, what are the possible remainders?
The fastest way to learn is to derive it yourself. Here's a starting point: what are the possible remainders of an integer upon division by $n$?
The remainder upon division by $n$ can never equal $n$ itself — what are the actual possible remainders?
items.attempt: I want to classify these numbers by remainder upon division by $n$: the remainder could be $0$ to $n$, that is $n+1$ values, so the $n+1$ numbers might each have a distinct remainder, and then no two would be congruent. I think the hypothesis is insufficient and we should take $n+2$ numbers instead. Is this correct?
items.planted_error: The number of remainder classes is wrong: remainders mod n are 0 to n-1, i.e. n classes (a remainder can't equal n); placing n+1 numbers into n classes forces a repeat, so the hypothesis is in fact sufficient.

items.reply: Start by computing the sum of all vertex degrees. Each edge contributes how much to this total?
Deriving it yourself is what will make you remember it. Here's a starting point: each edge contributes how much to the total degree sum?
The handshake lemma says the total degree sum is twice the number of edges — hence even. With that, what is the parity of the sum over the odd-degree vertices?
items.attempt: Each edge has two endpoints, so the sum of all vertex degrees equals the number of edges $|E|$. Suppose the number of odd-degree vertices is odd; then a sum of an odd number of odd numbers is odd, and adding the even sum of the even-degree vertices is still odd, but $|E|$ could be even — a contradiction. So the number of odd-degree vertices is even. Is my reasoning correct?
items.planted_error: The sum of degrees should be 2|E| (each edge contributes 2), not |E|; and "|E| could be even" yields no contradiction — the argument works precisely because the total always equals 2|E| and is thus even, so the original reasoning is logically incomplete.

items.reply: Start with the definition of linear dependence: suppose $c_1v_1+c_2v_2=0$. What happens when you left-multiply this equation by $A$?
Writing it yourself is what will make you remember it. Here's the first step: starting from $c_1v_1+c_2v_2=0$, what do you get after left-multiplying by $A$?
The conclusion is right, but the premise is wrong: "two nonzero vectors are linearly independent" is false. Can you think of a counterexample?
items.attempt: $v_1,v_2$ are eigenvectors, so by definition both are nonzero. Since both vectors are nonzero, the linear combination $c_1v_1+c_2v_2=0$ has only the solution $c_1=c_2=0$, so they are linearly independent. Is this correct?
items.planted_error: "Nonzero vectors must be linearly independent" is false (when v_2=2v_1 both are nonzero yet linearly dependent); the argument never uses the key condition lambda_1 != lambda_2 — an unused hypothesis usually signals a gap.

items.reply: A nilpotent operator satisfies $T^k=0$ for some $k$ — in this problem $T^2=0$. What does applying $T$ to an arbitrary vector $Tv$ give?
Writing it yourself is what will make you remember it. First: for any $v$, where does $Tv$ land?
The direction of the inclusion is backwards. $T^2=0$ means every $Tv$ lies where — which way does the inclusion go?
items.attempt: $T^2=0$ means the kernel is contained in the image, i.e. $\ker(T)\subseteq\operatorname{Im}(T)$, so $\operatorname{nullity}(T)\le\operatorname{rank}(T)$. By rank-nullity $\operatorname{rank}+\operatorname{nullity}=n$, giving $\operatorname{rank}(T)\ge\dfrac n2$. Is this correct?
items.planted_error: The inclusion direction is reversed: T^2=0 gives Im(T) subset of Ker(T) (any Tv is sent to 0 by T), not Ker subset of Im; so the conclusion's inequality is also reversed (correct is rank <= n/2).

items.reply: An eigenvalue $\lambda$ satisfies $Av=\lambda v$. To prove $\lambda$ is real, what kind of quantity do you get from taking the inner product of $v$ with $Av$?
Writing it yourself is what will make you remember it. Here's a starting point: left-multiplying the equation $Av=\lambda v$ by $v^*$ gives what?
The route is right, but the hypothesis "real symmetric" hasn't been used yet. Why is $v^TAv$ real — what property of $A$ guarantees that?
items.attempt: Suppose $Av=\lambda v$ with $v\ne0$. Left-multiply both sides by $v^T$ to get $v^TAv=\lambda v^Tv$. Since $v^Tv=\|v\|^2>0$ and $v^TAv$ is a real number, $\lambda=\dfrac{v^TAv}{v^Tv}$ is real. Is this correct?
items.planted_error: The eigenvector v may be complex: v^Tv is not necessarily ||v||^2 and can be 0 or complex (e.g. v=(1,i)^T gives v^Tv=0), and v^TAv need not be real. One must use the conjugate transpose v* and first argue that v*Av equals its own conjugate.
